This was actually about 3 years ago, but I'm only just now getting to the point where the denial is subsiding. I had just moved to Florida and I had never had to deal with cockroaches when I lived in Kansas. Over the first few weeks, I would see one in my bathroom. It was probably more than one, but I only saw one at a time. It would be on the floor, or in the bathtub. I saw it crawling over my soap bar, and I should have thrown the damn thing away, but I really feel like I was in denial that roaches were crawling around my apartment . A few days later, I noticed a few black spots on my soap bar, and some around my bathtub. I just rinsed it off the tub and went on with my day. But the black spots on the soap didn't come off as easy. After about a week or so, I was talking to a coworker who was also had a part time job as an exterminator. I told him about the cockroach, and he said "yeah, all they do is eat and shit all over the place." I blurted out "they shit all over the place?" He said "of course they do. Little black shits." I felt dirty. I had been using cockroach-shit covered soap for a week. The worst part is in the back of my mind, I knew that I had been the whole time, I was just too afraid of admitting that my apartment had a cockroach problem to deal with it. Never underestimate the power of denial.
